title: Your Loan EMIs and Savings Just Got an Update: Understanding the RBI's Latest Rate Hike
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has increased the key interest rate, called the repo rate, by 0.25%. This means the repo rate is now 5.50%, up from 5.25%.

faq.q: What is the current repo rate?
faq.a: As of October 7, 2026, the repo rate is 5.50%.

faq.q: When was the last time the RBI changed the repo rate before this?
faq.a: This is the first repo rate hike since February 2023.

faq.q: Will my home loan EMI definitely increase?
faq.a: If your home loan is on a floating rate linked to an external benchmark like the repo rate, it is highly likely your EMI will increase as banks pass on the higher cost.

"Calibrated tightening" means the RBI is focused on controlling inflation by gradually making money supply less easy, but it will do so in a measured way, watching economic data closely, rather than with aggressive, large steps.

faq.q: How often does the RBI review the repo rate?
faq.a: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) typically meets once every two months to review the economic situation and decide on the monetary policy, including the repo rate.
